newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Bank Austria to be privatised in steps. [CORRECTED 12:34 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Bank Austria to be privatised in steps. [CORRECTED 12:34 GMT]

text.p: The Austrian government said on Sunday it had struck a deal to sell flagship bank Creditanstalt to Bank Austria, agreeing on a series of measures for the merged bank to be eventually privatised.

According to the agreement, the state's 19 percent stake in Bank Austria would be floated immediately, while the 45 percent stake held by the City of Vienna's Anteilsverwaltung Zentralsparkasse (AVZ) foundation would be cut to below 20 percent within seven (corrects from five) years.
AVZ has to put 20 percent of its current stake in a fiduciary account immediately. Its total holding will be reduced to below 20 percent after another two years.

The reduction of AVZ's stake would be achieved through a series of capital increases in which the foundation would not take part, Finance Minister Viktor Klima told reporters after a marathon emergency meeting between coalition leaders.
Furthermore, AVZ must sell its 56 percent stake in savings bank GiroCredit AG immediately, Klima said.

As part of the deal Bank Austria agreed to buy out Creditanstalt's small shareholders at a small premium to the current price of the bank's ordinary voting shares, 30 percent of which are widely held.
Creditanstalt would remain independent for at least five years, the government said.
The two banks will have combined assets of about 14 billion schillings (1.26 billion) and a joint staff of about 15,000.
Klima said he would sign the sale contract immediately. -- Vienna newsroom, +431 531 12257
